es.summary: Pérdida involuntaria de orina al aumentar la presión intraabdominal, como al toser, reír o levantar peso. Se debe a debilidad del suelo pélvico y/o posición anormal de la vejiga.
key_points: Debilidad del suelo pélvico es la causa principal
Se desencadena por aumentos bruscos de presión intraabdominal
Diagnóstico clínico con historial y diario miccional
Primer línea de tratamiento: ejercicios de Kegel y cambios de estilo de vida

pathophysiology: Aumento de presión intraabdominal supera la resistencia del esfínter uretral externo
El suelo pélvico debilitado no cierra adecuadamente la uretra
Resultado: fuga de orina durante actividades que generan presión
signs_symptoms: Fugas de orina al toser, estornudar, reír o levantar objetos
Sensación de goteo inmediato tras el esfuerzo
No hay urgencia ni sensación de vejiga llena
Puede haber irritación perineal por humedad
diagnostics: Historia clínica y examen físico del suelo pélvico
treatment: Ejercicios de Kegel (reeducación del suelo pélvico)
Control de peso y reducción de consumo de cafeína/alcohol
Pessario uretral o dispositivo de soporte
Cirugía de sling uretral cuando los tratamientos conservadores fallan
complications: Irritación y dermatitis por uso prolongado de absorbentes
Infección del tracto urinario por estasis parcial
Aislamiento social y disminución de la calidad de vida
nursing_care: Evaluar patrón de micción y frecuencia de pérdidas
Inspeccionar piel perineal y registrar irritación
Registrar ingesta y salida de líquidos (ml)
Enseñar y supervisar ejercicios de Kegel
Proveer dispositivos absorbentes adecuados y cambiar cada 2‑4 h
patient_teaching: Practicar Kegel 3 series de 10 repeticiones, 3 veces al día
Mantener peso saludable y evitar levantar >10 kg sin apoyo
Limitar cafeína, alcohol y alimentos irritantes
Usar ropa interior absorbente y cambiarla frecuentemente
Programar micción cada 2‑3 h para evitar sobrecarga

care_plans.diagnosis: Riesgo de desequilibrio de volumen de líquidos
outcomes: Volumen de líquidos: mantener balance hídrico dentro de límites normales durante 24 h
Control de la incontinencia: reducir episodios de pérdida de orina a <1 por día

interventions.action: Evaluar ingesta y salida de líquidos cada turno
interventions.rationale: Permite detectar déficit o exceso de volumen relacionado con pérdidas urinarias

interventions.action: Registrar frecuencia y cantidad de pérdidas en diario miccional
interventions.rationale: Facilita la identificación de patrones y efectividad de intervenciones

interventions.action: Enseñar ejercicios de Kegel y supervisar su correcta ejecución
interventions.rationale: Fortalece el suelo pélvico y reduce la fuga de orina

interventions.action: Aplicar crema protectora cutánea en zona perineal según necesidad
interventions.rationale: Previene irritación y pérdida de integridad cutánea

interventions.action: Educar sobre control de peso y reducción de cafeína
interventions.rationale: Disminuye presión intraabdominal y mejora control urinario

related_to: pérdida de orina durante actividad física
evidenced_by: evita actividades sociales por temor a fuga
outcomes: Capacidad para realizar actividades de la vida diaria sin pérdida de orina en 80 % de intentos
Participación en ejercicio leve (caminar 30 min) al menos 3 veces/semana

interventions.action: Evaluar nivel de actividad y describir situaciones que provocan fuga
interventions.rationale: Identifica desencadenantes y permite planificar adaptaciones

interventions.action: Implementar programa progresivo de ejercicios de Kegel y fortalecimiento lumbar
interventions.rationale: Mejora soporte uretral y tolerancia al esfuerzo

interventions.action: Planificar horarios de micción antes de actividades programadas
interventions.rationale: Reduce la cantidad de orina residual y riesgo de fuga

interventions.action: Proveer dispositivos de soporte (pessario) si es necesario
interventions.rationale: Ofrece soporte mecánico durante actividades que aumentan presión

interventions.action: Fomentar participación gradual en actividades sociales y registrar progreso
interventions.rationale: Promueve adaptación y disminuye miedo al ejercicio

en.summary: Unintentional loss of urine when intraabdominal pressure increases, such as during coughing, laughing, or lifting weight. It is caused by pelvic floor weakness and/or abnormal bladder positioning.
key_points: Pelvic floor weakness is the primary cause
Triggered by sudden increases in intraabdominal pressure
Clinical diagnosis with history and voiding diary
First-line treatment: Kegel exercises and lifestyle changes

pathophysiology: Increased intraabdominal pressure exceeds the resistance of the external urethral sphincter
A weakened pelvic floor fails to close the urethra properly
Result: urine leakage during activities that generate pressure
signs_symptoms: Urine leakage when coughing, sneezing, laughing, or lifting objects
No urgency or feeling of a full bladder
diagnostics: Medical history and pelvic floor physical exam
treatment: Weight control and reduction of caffeine/alcohol intake
Urethral sling surgery when conservative treatments fail
complications: Irritation and dermatitis from prolonged use of absorbents
Urinary tract infection from partial stasis
Social isolation and reduced quality of life
nursing_care: Assess voiding pattern and frequency of losses
Inspect perineal skin and document irritation
Provide appropriate absorbent devices and change every 2‑4 h
patient_teaching: Practice Kegel 3 sets of 10 repetitions, 3 times daily
Maintain healthy weight and avoid lifting >10 kg without support
Limit caffeine, alcohol, and irritant foods
Use absorbent underwear and change frequently
Schedule voiding every 2‑3 h to avoid overload

outcomes: Fluid volume: maintain fluid balance within normal limits for 24 h
Incontinence control: reduce episodes of urine loss to <1 per day

interventions.action: Assess fluid intake and output each shift
interventions.rationale: Detects deficits or excess related to urinary losses

interventions.action: Document frequency and amount of losses in voiding diary
interventions.rationale: Facilitates pattern identification and intervention effectiveness

interventions.action: Teach Kegel exercises and supervise correct performance
interventions.rationale: Strengthens pelvic floor and reduces urine leakage

interventions.action: Apply protective skin cream to perineal area as needed
interventions.rationale: Prevents irritation and maintains skin integrity

interventions.action: Educate on weight control and caffeine reduction
interventions.rationale: Reduces intraabdominal pressure and improves urinary control

evidenced_by: avoids social activities due to fear of leakage
outcomes: Ability to perform activities of daily living without urine loss in 80 % of attempts
Participation in light exercise (walking 30 min) at least 3 times per week

interventions.action: Assess activity level and describe situations that provoke leakage
interventions.rationale: Identifies triggers and allows planning of adaptations

interventions.action: Implement progressive Kegel and lumbar strengthening program
interventions.rationale: Improves urethral support and tolerance to exertion

interventions.action: Plan voiding schedules before planned activities
interventions.rationale: Reduces residual urine and leakage risk

interventions.action: Provide support devices (pessary) if necessary
interventions.rationale: Offers mechanical support during activities that increase pressure

interventions.action: Encourage gradual participation in social activities and track progress
interventions.rationale: Promotes adaptation and reduces fear of exercise

summary.0.quote: Stress incontinence happens when stress or pressure on your bladder causes you to leak urine.

summary.1.quote: Causes include weak pelvic floor muscles and the bladder being out of its normal position.

key_points.2.quote: Your health care provider may use many tools to make a diagnosis: A medical history, which includes asking about your symptoms.

sections.risk_factors.0.quote: In adults, you are at higher risk of developing UI if you: Are female, especially after going through pregnancy, childbirth, and/or menopause Are older.

sections.signs_symptoms.0.quote: Stress incontinence happens when stress or pressure on your bladder causes you to leak urine.

sections.diagnostics.0.quote: A physical exam, which can include a rectal exam. Women may also get a pelvic exam.
